subject: Cloudline discovery — deployment constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@cloudline.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 15:02:14 +0000
Subject: Cloudline discovery — deployment constraints & next steps

Hi Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have a single source of truth. Please correct anything I’ve misunderstood.

Summary of pain / goals you shared
- Intermittent but severe tail-latency on your current hosted endpoints (spikes to 800–1200ms p95 on 512-token prompts during batch jobs).
- Cost unpredictability under periodic batch ingestion and daytime conversational traffic.
- Need multi-region presence for APAC customers, plus a VPC/private control plane for regulated PII pipelines.

SLO targets you mentioned
- Interactive product: target p95 <= 100ms for ~512-token generation on high-priority routes.
- Throughput baseline: ~200 sustained qps across the US region; bursts up to ~1k rps during peak pipelines.
- Failure tolerance: autoscale + graceful fallback to smaller variant when capacity constrained.

Model & technical constraints
- Primary model family: planning to evaluate an open Llama-3 70B quantized candidate for quality.
- KV cache is important for latency on session-based flows — warm cache/affinity will matter.
- Some workloads will require 4k+ context; we should verify memory footprint and acceptable quantization.

Initial topology thoughts (we'll confirm on deep-dive)
- Dedicated capacity in us-east with a small regional burst pool in us-west for redundancy.
- Prefix caching in the serving tier + sticky routing for sessions.
- Private control plane (VPC) + KMS integration for keys/audit.

Next steps we agreed
1) I’ll send our SOC2 summary and a draft mutual action plan (attached).
2) Technical deep-dive with infra + runtime engineers to map topology and run a capacity estimate (proposed week of Oct 12; suggested slot Tue Oct 13 16:00 PT).
3) You’ll share a sample traffic trace and a list of top 20 latency-sensitive routes + any compliance docs procurement needs.

Attachments: Cloudline-MAP-draft.pdf (mutual action plan draft), SOC2-summary.pdf (high level).

If that looks right, let me know if Tue 10/13 16:00 PT works for the deep-dive and I’ll lock in invites and prep notes for the team.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Tom Li <tom.li@cloudline.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudline.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 18:05:30 +0000
Subject: Re: Cloudline discovery — deployment constraints & next steps

Thanks Hannah — this is exactly the right level of detail. Couple clarifications:  
- Burst expectations: we commonly see bursts up to ~1k rps for short (1–3 minute) windows when our batch pipelines kick in — good to call out.
- For the model, quality is the priority but cost matters; we are open to a hybrid approach (larger model for customer-facing routes, distilled variant for background jobs).

Tue 10/13 16:00 PT works for our infra lead (I’ll confirm their calendar).

On procurement: we’d prefer a 90-day pilot window with a PO, and we’ll need standard security attestations and a copy of your Data Processing Addendum. I CC’d procurement.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Tom
Tom Li
Head of Platform Engineering, Cloudline Systems
Tom.Li@cloudline.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Cloudline discovery — prep + asks (internal)

Forwarding the thread — internal asks below. This is a good-fit opportunity (multi-region, dedicated capacity; likely a pilot + reserved). Please treat as high priority.

Prep asks for Tue 10/13 deep-dive:
- Rishi: can you produce a capacity estimate (sustained 200 qps / burst 1k rps; 512–4k contexts; quantized 70B candidate) using the attached capacity_estimate_template.xlsx? Focus on node counts for dedicated pools, expected p95 under continuous batching, and fallback model sizing.
- Vanessa: please pull SOC2 artefacts and the minimal network/VPC diagram we’d send to customers (KMS integration notes). Also draft a short pricing outline for a 90-day pilot + annual reserved BW.
- Ops: plan to propose 3 topology options (single-region dedicated + burst pool; multi-region active-active; lightweight hybrid with hosted fallback).

Attachments: capacity_estimate_template.xlsx (fill and return).

I’ll own the call agenda and client alignment. Will loop in Product Engineering if we need kernel/quantization tradeoff input.

Thanks — Hannah

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Cloudline discovery — prep + asks (internal)

On it. Filling the template now and attaching the initial capacity CSV (capacity_estimate_cloudline.csv) with three costed topology options:
- Option A: Single-region dedicated (baseline) — meets p95 90–110ms with reserved GPUs + prefix cache; sustainable 250 qps, bursts to 800 rps with burst pool.
- Option B: Regional active-passive w/ warm cache — better tail behavior for APAC; slightly higher cost.
- Option C: Hybrid hosted fallback — lowers committed spend; falls back to smaller quantized model under sustained load.

I’ll present the numbers on Tue and include recommended warmup strategies for KV cache.

-Rishi
Attachment: capacity_estimate_cloudline.csv
